title: Devon’s libraries are limited, plus a Sheffield switcheroo
author: Ian Anstice / The Library Campaign

editorial.text: The name “Libraries Unlimited” for Devon’s non-profit trust is starting to look like a misnomer after it announced a plan to remove all its 19 current library supervisors and replace them with just 10 “library and community managers”. There’s been a lot of negative publicity about it in the local press this week and with good reason: :the council had only just agreed to invest £1 million in the service, for one thing, and the fact that some of these library supervisors look like they are downright loved by their local communities is another. And, to me anyway, the way the trust says this reduction will make things “more resilient” looks like a slap in the face for those whose jobs are currently in danger. Branch managers are the face of the library to their community, with a good one being an absolute dynamo. In reality, it’s hard to see how this move is anything but a cost-cutting measure. Avoid the temptation of management-speak and remember real people are involved – your colleagues for goodness sake – would be my advice to the trust’s management. Then on to Sheffield Central. This was my public library when I was doing a MA in Librarianship in the city and I remember it well. It was a beautiful building but even back then (1994) it was clear that it had limited funding, as there almost no new books on its shelves. News stories since 2010 suggest things have not improved much, with a 2017 article speculating on it being sold off to a Chinese-owned hotel chain and, six years later, reports that cracks in the building led to a three-metre “exclusion zone” around it. So this week’s news that the site of it and the town’s gallery being switched does not necessarily strike me as bad news, other than in terms of nostalgia and pondering about how this will affect its listed building status. It’s now down, as ever, to funding. Will the money come through? And if so will the city have the money to maintain the library sufficiently so as not need to sell or tape it off? The designs give some hope. There’s no cracks shown in any of them.
